widget.label: Human verification
widget.failed: The verification did not go through. Try again.
widget.unavailable: The verification service could not be reached. Try again in a moment.
widget.loadFailed: The verification could not load. Reload the page, or allow challenges.cloudflare.com if a blocker stopped it.

admin.title: Cloudflare Turnstile
admin.intro: Asks visitors to show they are human on the sign-in, registration, password reset and invitation forms. It is off until a site key and a secret key are saved and the switch is on.
admin.enabledDesc: While this is on, signing in, registering, asking for a password reset and accepting an invitation all need the check.
admin.fromEnv: This configuration comes from the environment (TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY and TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY). The fields stay read-only until you take it over here.
admin.overridesEnv: These settings override TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY and TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY in the environment.
admin.secretKeep: Leave empty to keep the stored secret key
admin.secretSet: A secret key is stored. It is encrypted at rest and never sent back to the browser, so this field is always empty.
admin.secretUnset: No secret key is stored. A new site key needs its own secret key.
admin.secretUnreadable: The stored secret key can no longer be decrypted, which usually means AUTH_SECRET changed. The check stays off until you type it again.
admin.secretFromEnv: The secret key comes from TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY and is not shown.
admin.savedOn: The forms now ask for the check. Try signing in from a private window before you sign out.
admin.savedOff: The forms no longer ask for the check.

invalid.invalid-site-key: That site key does not look like a Cloudflare key (letters, digits, - and _ only).
invalid.invalid-secret: That secret key does not look like a Cloudflare key (letters, digits, - and _ only).
invalid.site-key-required: Turning the check on needs a site key.
invalid.secret-required: Turning the check on needs a secret key. A changed site key needs its own secret key too.
invalid.secret-rejected: Cloudflare rejected this secret key, so nothing was saved: with a wrong secret key nobody could sign in, you included.
invalid.unreachable: Cloudflare could not be reached to confirm the secret key, so nothing was saved. Try again.
invalid.rate-limited: Too many requests to Cloudflare from this account. Wait a few minutes.

admin.revertedDesc: The values saved here were removed.
admin.testDesc: Sends the secret key (the one typed above, otherwise the one in use) to Cloudflare and shows whether Cloudflare accepts it. Nothing is saved.
admin.testAlwaysPasses: This is one of Cloudflare's test secret keys: it lets every visitor through. Use it only to try things out.

testError.no-secret: There is no secret key to test. Type one above.
testError.invalid-secret: That secret key does not look like a Cloudflare key (letters, digits, - and _ only).
testError.unreachable: Cloudflare could not be reached from this server.
testError.rate-limited: Too many requests to Cloudflare from this account. Wait a few minutes.

admin.howTo: In the Cloudflare dashboard open Turnstile and add a widget. List every host name this panel is reached on (this one is {host}), keep the Managed mode, then copy the site key and the secret key here.
admin.testKeys: To try it out, Cloudflare's test keys work on any host, localhost included: site key 1x00000000000000000000AA with secret key 1x0000000000000000000000000000000AA lets everyone through, secret key 2x0000000000000000000000000000000AA refuses everyone.
admin.lockout: Keep this tab signed in until you have signed in once from a private window: a widget that does not match its host names would keep everyone out.
